newsitem.title: USA: Citizens sells service to Bank United.
newsitem.headline: Citizens sells service to Bank United.

text.p: Citizens Finanacial Group Inc Monday said Houston-based Bank United Corp will acquire $3.8 billion of mortgage and investor services from Citizens' for an undisclosed price.
After the sale, Citizens will record a one-time gain of $42 million, $21 million of which Citizens said it reported in its results for the quarter ending December 31, 1996.

Bank United will purchase Citizens' Federal Home Loan Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae), Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp (Freddie Mac) and Government National Mortgage Association, or Ginnie Mae, services from Citizens.
The sale was approved by the U.S. Federal Trade Commission under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Act, and is expected to be completed by the end of the first quarter of 1997.

Citizens said the sale completes its previously announced decision to sell its $8.8 billion mortgage servicing portfolio, close wholesale mortgage offices in the southeast and northeast and focus on retail mortgage origination through its Citizens Bank offices in its New England franchise.
Citizens is 76.5 percent owned by the Royal Bank of Scotland PLC, with the remainder held by The Bank of Ireland.
